chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rabi'i ibn Abdullah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to order the children to combine between Maghrib and 'Isha, and he would say: 'It is better than them sleeping through it.'
ai.seo_question: How should children be taught to combine Maghrib and Isha prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Sajjad (AS) instructed children to combine Maghrib and 'Isha to prevent them from missing the prayer due to sleep, illustrating the practical pedagogical approach of gradual integration (Tadrij) in Shia fiqh. This narration underscores the principle that maintaining the habit of prayer in childhood is prioritized over strict adherence to individual prayer times, serving as a foundational step for their eventual obligation (Taklif).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzaan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,
‘It was so that Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws used to order the children to gather between Al-Maghrib and Al-Isha (Salāts), and heasws was be saying: ‘It is better than being asleep (ignorant) from it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib‘i ibn ‘Abd Allah from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “
Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would instruct children to perform Salah (prayer) of al-Maghrib and al-‘Isha’ soon, one after the other, saying that it is better for them than falling asleep.”
